newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher Thursday, with technology shares boosted by the $6.6 billion merger of 3Com Corp and U.S. Robotics Corp, analysts said.

They said markets were likely to shrug off Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning that share prices may be overvalued. The Dow Industrials fell more than 100 points following his remarks Wednesday, but later staged a partial recovery. The index closed down 55 points at 6983.
"It's really rather remarkable how Wall Street has taken the Greenspan thing relatively in stride," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfallia Research, said markets were likely to focus on economic data due today, looking for indicators on inflation and a possible Fed tightening of interest rates.
Among the data, jobless claims for the week ended February 22 are due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. Economists' consensus forecast is for 310,000 claims, up slightly from the previous week.
A report on help-wanted advertising is due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
"If we see any strength in that help-wanted index, people might just reflect on Mr. Greenspan's theme that good things don't last forever," Cardillo said.

Analysts said high-technology stocks were likely to be boosted by the merger of 3Com, a computer network company, and modem giant U.S. Robotics. The deal would create a counterweight to Cisco Systems Inc.
"This might revive enthusiasm in the tech sector," Cardillo said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average rose 30.64 points, or 0.16 percent, to close at 19,021.56.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 8.2 points at 4337.5.
U.S. shares traded in London were steady to slightly higher.
The dollar dived more than a yen in Tokyo and softened against the mark and yen in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were off 8/32 to yield 6.79. The Standard & Poors 500 futures index was up 1.55 to 805.30.
